target.title: fix(update): keep self-updates on the running install's global root
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw update` could report success after updating a different global package tree when the running install and the npm command on `PATH` belonged to different Node installations. The process that invoked the update would remain on the old version, and a Homebrew upgrade could later delete the accidentally created Cellar tree.

The reproduced case used an nvm-owned OpenClaw install with a service environment whose npm probe resolved under Homebrew's versioned Cellar prefix.

## Why This Change Was Made

Once npm ownership is established and the resolved package root has a valid npm global-prefix layout, the updater now treats that running prefix as authoritative. This matches npm's documented layout (`<prefix>/lib/node_modules` on Unix and `<prefix>/node_modules` on Windows) and keeps staging, verification, atomic swap, and the post-update doctor on the tree that actually supplied OpenClaw.

When the supplied root is not a global npm package root, the existing `npm root -g` behavior remains unchanged. That boundary preserves legitimate nvm, fnm, asdf, Volta, and `n` roots for git-to-package installs and avoids mistaking a local `node_modules/openclaw` dependency for a global install. pnpm and bun selection are unchanged. Scoped npm package roots follow the same rule.

Official npm layout contract: https://docs.npmjs.com/files/folders.html

## User Impact

Self-updates in mixed Node/npm environments now mutate the running OpenClaw installation instead of silently creating or refreshing a second copy. Existing installs without a recognized running global npm root continue to use npm's own configured global root.

No config, environment variable, dependency, or migration is added.

## Evidence

- Before: the incident handoff showed the running nvm package at `2026.5.28`, while the update command staged and installed under `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.1/lib/node_modules`; the target tree did not previously exist.
- Live macOS proof from the contributor: with the same skewed PATH, `openclaw update --yes` changed the nvm-owned running package from `2026.6.9` to `2026.6.11`; the Cellar root remained empty.
- Exact reviewed head: `f17f77ba41c66130572c9916a36131dc2434fb87`.
- Sanitized contributor-code proof: AWS Crabbox run `run_50739d922bcb`, public network, no Tailscale, empty instance profile, no credential hydration.
  - `pnpm test src/infra/update-global.test.ts src/infra/update-runner.test.ts src/cli/update-cli.test.ts`: 273 passed across the infra and CLI shards on Linux / Node 24.
  - `pnpm check:changed -- src/infra/update-global.ts src/infra/update-global.test.ts`: passed production and test typechecks, changed-file lint (0 warnings/errors), dependency guards, runtime import-cycle guard, and all remaining selected lanes.
- Focused formatting: `oxfmt --check src/infra/update-global.ts src/infra/update-global.test.ts` passed.
- Fresh autoreview after the final refactor: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

Related: #98618 describes a similar multiple-install version-skew symptom, but remains open because its exact install shape has not been proven to be this path.
